fr:title.text: Intrinsic hylomorphisms: the output carrier is the specification

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Intrinsic hylomorphisms: the output carrier is the specification

fr:mainmatter.html:p: The recurring pattern across the examples: index the Löb recursion base by the data the correctness statement mentions, and make the output carrier the specification itself. The algebra is then forced to produce the proof, so correctness falls out of hylo by type. The computed value still reduces by refl --- the proof sits in the second projection.
The roster (Direct.Examples):

html:ul.html:li: GCD --- Euclid; carrier Σ d, isGCD m n d, algebra is zeroGCD/stepGCD. Recaptures the AUW intrinsically-recursive GCD.
Karatsuba --- carrier Σ p, p ≡ x · y; the schoolbook identity discharged by solveℕ! and truncated-subtraction cancellation.
Quicksort --- bag-indexed, so permutation is definitional bag-equality; carrier Σ ys, Sorted ys × fromList ys ≡ b, a sorted permutation by type.
Binary search --- input a Sorted xs proof, output Dec (Member xs), returning Maybe (Fin (length xs)).
Bellman--Ford --- the carrier bundles each distance with optimality (a lower bound that is attained).

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Non-verified demonstrations also present: Towers of Hanoi, CYK parsing, Ackermann.

Every hylomorphism example currently hand-writes its functor and its contractive strength (the δ). Local contractivity should instead be a closed class with combinators, so larger contractive maps are assembled from smaller ones and δ is derived.
The closure conditions --- the guarded/metric semantics of the later modality:

html:ul.html:li: a recursive position guarded by \triangleright is contractive --- a bare variable is only non-expansive;
sums, products, and linear/tensor products preserve contractivity positionwise;
composition with a non-expansive functor preserves contractivity on either side.

fr:mainmatter.html:p: These are exactly the constructors of the grammar functor language, which is a syntactic form of this calculus. Pairs with the ranked-container interface.

fr:title.text: Directions for direct-category recursion in Cubical Agda

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Directions for direct-category recursion in Cubical Agda

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Feature requests and directions building on the lob branch: where the Löb-recursion and intrinsic-hylomorphism machinery can go next.

A calculus of contractive functors. Make local contractivity a closed class with combinators --- constants, the guard, sums, products, composition --- and package the functor plus strength as a ranked-container interface so instances stop hand-writing it. This generalises to the indexed-inductive grammars, whose rank is string length.

The recursion-scheme zoo. hylo is the only scheme so far. Add catamorphisms, anamorphisms, para/apomorphisms, and especially histomorphisms (course-of-values recursion) --- the strict-downset sieve already exposes every smaller value, so course-of-values falls out directly. Dynamorphisms would package dynamic programming as a scheme.
Corecursion and streams. Dualise: guarded corecursion via the later modality, streams and processes productive by construction, anamorphisms as the dual of hylo. Continues the in-flight streams work.
Cost-aware recursion. Carry a cost in the carrier so the well-founded measure doubles as an intrinsic complexity bound (compare calf); recover amortized analysis through the potential.
More intrinsic algorithms. Broaden the roster: edit distance / LCS / knapsack (DP), mergesort, intrinsic Dijkstra, full CYK returning a parse derivation.
Effectful hylomorphisms. Recursion in a Kleisli category --- partial, nondeterministic, probabilistic --- reusing the existing FreeSubst/Kleisli machinery.

Semantics and higher structure. Reedy categories (semisimplicial and simplicial diagrams), internal guarded recursive types \mu /\nu , and the \square /\Diamond modalities as the internal language of the topos of trees.
Upstreaming. The WFOrder, pullbackWFOrder, direct-category, and Löb kit (bases) is broadly useful and is a candidate to merge into agda/cubical.

fr:title.text: Fold shared integer-halving into a nat-utility home

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Fold shared integer-halving into a nat-utility home

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Karatsuba (halving over the \Sigma -order) and binary search (halving over the recursive order) each define integer halving with a strict-decrease bound. They should share one definition, but Data.Nat.More is already the tropical-cost semiring, so there is no clean home.

Options: rename Data.Nat.More to Data.Nat.Cost and open a genuine nat-utility More, or a small Data.Nat.Half. Unifying also wants Karatsuba switched to the recursive <, which simplifies its coalgebra by dropping the <→Wo< conversion.

fr:title.text: Grammar indexed inductives are the indexed, string-ranked containers

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Grammar indexed inductives are the indexed, string-ranked containers

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Does the ranked-container interface generalise to the indexed inductives in the grammars codebase? Yes --- and it is already half-built.

In grammars-and-semantic-actions, a grammar is String → Type, and Grammar.Inductive.Functor is a strictly-positive polynomial-functor language: constants k, recursive references Var, indexed sums ⊕e and products &e, and linear/cartesian products ⊗e/&e2. Its μ F is the indexed inductive (initial algebra), with rec/ind. That is precisely an indexed (multi-sorted) container --- the ranked container moved from one object to X-indexed grammars.

The rank is string length. Grammar.Later guards a grammar behind consuming a nonempty prefix, built over Cubical.Induction.WellFounded. So a functor is ranked / locally contractive exactly when every Var sits under \triangleright --- the same guardedness as the direct-category order. The combinators are its k/⊕e/&e/⊗e constructors.

The gsa-lob / gsa-well-founded-recursion worktrees and this branch are the same theorem over two sites --- strings versus a general direct category. The goal is to unify them into one Löb/hylo kit with two instantiations; CYK (roster) is the toy case, parsing ranked by span length.

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Untracked work on the lob branch: directed-graph, weighted-graph, and shortest-path instances, plus shortest-path and stream examples and a perf test. The cost semiring already moved to Data.Nat.More (min-plus / tropical, with its \sqsubseteq order).
Goal: an intrinsic shortest-path in the style of Bellman--Ford over a proper (weighted) graph API, and streams as coalgebras of the later modality. Not yet building end-to-end.
Direct.Base exports pullbackWFOrder Wo isSetA meas, pulling a well-founded order back along a measure into its domain. Every base used by the examples is a one-liner over it.

html:ul.html:li: Instances.ListByLength --- lists over a carrier, ordered by length.
Instances.Bag --- finite multisets, ordered by size.
Instances.Nat and the lexicographic Direct.Product --- naturals and pairs.

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Instances.Poset was generalised to WFOrder ℓ ℓ' so these bases are level-polymorphic. The single-use NatPair was inlined and deleted. Shared list predicates All, Sorted, and lookupD live in Data.List.More.

fr:title.text: The lob branch: direct categories, Löb induction, and intrinsic hylomorphisms

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: The lob branch: direct categories, Löb induction, and intrinsic hylomorphisms

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Summary of the lob branch's diffs to main: a self-contained account of well-founded recursion in Cubical Agda, from categorical foundations up to concrete algorithms verified by type. Target: Max New's guarded/direct-category development.
The branch stacks three layers.

html:ul.html:li: Presheaves are monadic and comonadic over families --- the (co)Eilenberg--Moore foundation the guarded modality rests on.
Direct categories, the later modality, and Löb induction --- the recursion principle.
Intrinsic hylomorphisms: the output carrier is the specification --- the payoff, a roster of verified algorithms.

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Infrastructure: measure-ordered direct categories via pullbackWFOrder.
Where next: directions for direct-category recursion.
Open threads: a shared half has no clean home; intrinsic shortest-path and streams are in flight.

fr:title.text: Direct categories, the later modality, and Löb induction

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Direct categories, the later modality, and Löb induction

fr:mainmatter.html:p: A direct category carries a well-founded degree functor (Direct.Base: directness as a displayed StructureOver plus GlobalSection; Direct.WellFounded). The strict-downset sieve of maps of strictly smaller degree (Direct.StrictDownset) defines the later modality \triangleright as a presheaf endofunctor with a next unit.

Löb induction is the guarded fixed point: a map \triangleright A \to A has a unique fixed point, computing definitionally because WFOrder lives in the Eq-world. Exposed as a presheaf-level löb and a family-level strong recursion löbStr.

Direct.LocallyContractive: a locally contractive functor is a \Sigma of an object-action and a \triangleright -hom action; its hylo is Löb applied to the fused (co)algebra. Direct.Product gives lexicographic products of direct categories.
Notation: families are objects of the family category, exposed as Löb.Fam, so instances never respell ob → hSet by hand.
